hypothesis: A bounded exact-cover search that allows all seven baseline rows to change simultaneously will find a scope-111 DTS within a small L-infinity neighborhood, even though changing only the first row against six fixed rows found no completion.
rationale: The clamped scope-111 baseline has five duplicate differences, and the prior radius-10 search varied only row 0. The missing repair may require coordinated changes in multiple rows. Enumerating every valid Golomb row in a radius-3 neighborhood for all seven rows and solving pairwise difference-mask compatibility directly tests that mechanism without stochastic pool starvation or a monolithic integer solver.
expected_information_gain: Distinguishes a local coordinated-repair possibility from the previously tested one-row neighborhood and broad direct solver formulations; a complete exhaustive negative result would bound this concrete neighborhood.
method: For each of the seven published scope-112 rows, enumerate all 5-coordinate perturbations with deltas in [-3,3], retain rows with scope <=111 and 15 internally unique differences, deduplicate by difference mask, then run reversible DFS for one mutually disjoint mask per row. Validate any complete assignment with verify_dts.verify. Use radius 3, scope limit 111, a 120-second wall budget, and a 5,000,000-node cap.
metric: complete target assignment, exact row-pool sizes, DFS depth/nodes, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete assignment accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; an exhausted neighborhood is only a local structural negative result and does not imply global infeasibility.

configuration.enumeration: all 7^5 coordinate perturbations per baseline row

kill_condition: Stop after a validator-valid complete assignment, after exhaustive DFS, or at 120 seconds/5,000,000 nodes; do not generalize a bounded-neighborhood failure to the global problem.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and validator-valid

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: new information only if coordinated all-row neighborhood differs materially

interpretation: The all-row radius-3 neighborhood generated substantial valid candidate pools and the exact compatibility DFS reached depth 5, but it stopped at the 5,000,000-node cap before exhausting the neighborhood. No candidate was produced and no global infeasibility inference is warranted.
what_was_learned: Coordinated all-row repair has a materially larger finite search space than the prior one-row test; the simple DFS representation is the bottleneck, not an empty candidate neighborhood. A candidate-level exact-cover solver is justified as the next representation.
recommended_next_action: If a witness is found, freeze and independently/adversarially verify it; if the neighborhood is exhausted without a witness, pause local repair and require a broader structural construction family.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the prior fixed-six-row radius-10 enumeration: all seven rows are variable, candidate pools are exhaustive within a bounded L-infinity neighborhood, and the global compatibility search is exact rather than sampled.
